title: ～だろう — “probably ～”
summary: The plain-style way of guessing “probably ～.” It is the casual counterpart of でしょう and is used in monologues, with close friends, and in writing.

patterns.form: 動詞・い形容詞の普通形＋だろう
patterns.gloss: Verb or い-adjective plain form + だろう (食べるだろう, 高いだろう)

patterns.form: 名詞・な形容詞（語幹）＋だろう
patterns.gloss: Noun or な-adjective stem + だろう (先生だろう, 静かだろう)

body.p: だろう is the guessing form of だ. It attaches straight to plain forms (食べる, 高い). After a noun or な-adjective, no extra だ is inserted (先生だろう).
It is used for predictions and for guesses about things you cannot see for sure. In speech, だろうね or だろう？ can also ask for the listener’s agreement.
The meaning is the same, but だろう is plain. When you speak politely, especially to someone senior, use でしょう.

examples.ja: 明日（あした）は晴（は）れるだろう。
examples.tr: It will probably be sunny tomorrow.

examples.ja: この店（みせ）は高（たか）いだろう。
あの人（ひと）は先生（せんせい）だろう。
examples.tr: That person is probably a teacher.

pitfalls: Do not use it for facts you know for sure. For certain things, state them plainly with です.
Do not add だ before だろう after a noun or な-adjective (not 先生だだろう).
